questions.question: One benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is:

options.text: Your motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
Maintenance checks take a lot of time.
Maintenance checks can prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will ride well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will continue to run like new. Regular maintenance checks should be part of your routine care.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of a lane?
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the center of each lane. Motorcycles can usually ride safely on this strip when roads are dry.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get away from them.

questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes when safe and allow them to go ahead. Speeding up will only make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: A plastic face shield on a helmet protects you from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and rocks thrown by other vehicles. It also protects you in a crash.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) are designed to:

options.text: Stop your wheels from locking up and skidding.
Prevent brakes from working on dry roads.
Tell you when your brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop your wheels from locking up and skidding.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheel lock-up and skidding during emergency braking. When sensors detect that a wheel is about to lock, the system releases and reapplies brake pressure to keep maximum braking power.

questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer than usual to stop, you should:

options.text: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
Stay closer to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, increase your distance from other vehicles. If your bike needs more time to stop, you need more space between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down later than usual.
Try to fit into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. It will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more space to stop. Ride slowly, start slowing sooner, leave more space between vehicles, and wait for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping a riding group small is:

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic.
A small group can break traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always be catching up to the group.
It is hard to keep track of everyone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic.
questions.explanation: Small groups are easier for cars to pass, less likely to be separated by traffic or lights, and don't put pressure on slower riders to catch up.

questions.question: You should not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may need to use that lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle can also block your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have blind spots that are so small they are not a problem.
Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular scanning routine.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: A helmet greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not block your side vision.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when needed, slow down, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oil, shade, dirt, gravel, and bridges—these reduce traction.

questions.question: If you wait one hour to ride after one alcoholic drink:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and driving.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour. But alcohol can build up in your system even with one drink per hour, and it can still affect your riding ability.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, clothing:

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not fully cover your arms or legs.
Should not include a jacket in warm weather.
Can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: The right clothing provides vital protection in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Clothes should fit snugly so they do not flap, but loose enough to allow movement.

questions.question: Which of the following does not protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, ankle-covering boots, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen often, so don't worry about them.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can be fatal.

questions.question: For the best protection, your helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious defects.

questions.question: To prevent injury when riding on a slippery surface, a motorcyclist should:
questions.explanation: Decrease your speed on slippery surfaces. Sudden moves on slippery roads can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to escape slippery pavement.

questions.question: Turn signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are not important since motorcycles are small.
Are very important to warn other drivers of your plans.
Should not be used if no vehicles are nearby.
Are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important to warn other drivers of your plans.
questions.explanation: As a motorcyclist, you are vulnerable. Always use turn signals to alert others to your plans. Use them any time you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up makes them tailgate at a higher speed, increasing danger.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes on both the front and rear wheels.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes on both the front and rear wheels.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes. One brake controls the front wheel, and the other controls the rear wheel.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle operator should be ready for:

options.text: A parked car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
Other drivers to see the motorcycle and stay out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, a parked car may suddenly pull into traffic. It is safer for a motorcyclist to ride on the left side of their lane when parked cars are on the right. This creates more space between the motorcycle and any sudden movements.

questions.question: Which color is best to wear to be seen while riding?
questions.explanation: Bright colors like orange, red, yellow, and green make you easier to see on a motorcycle. Wear bright clothing at any time of day.

questions.question: What helps other drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight at intersections makes you more visible. Also, position your motorcycle in your lane so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: For the best protection, a helmet should:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all around your head and have no damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.
